chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn 'Abd al-Ghaffar, who said:

The Abbasids came to Salih ibn Wasif, and Salih ibn Ali and others from those deviating from this direction also came to Salih ibn Wasif when he had imprisoned Abu Muhammad عليه السلام. So Salih said to them, “What can I do? I had assigned over him two men from the most evil persons I could find, but they have come to a tremendous state through worship, salat (prayer), and fasting.” So I said to the two of them, “What is his condition?” They said, “What can be said about a man who fasts by day and stands the whole night, not speaking and not occupying himself with anything else? Whenever we look at him, our limbs tremble, and there enters into us something we cannot control within ourselves.” So when they heard that, they departed disappointed.

key_terms.ارْتَعَدَتْ فَرَائِصُنَا: our limbs trembled in awe and fear
key_terms.الْعَبَّاسِيُّونَ: the Abbasid authorities and their associates
key_terms.الْعِبَادَةِ: devotional worship and servitude to Allah
key_terms.الْمُنْحَرِفِينَ: those who had deviated in opposition to this cause

ai.seo_question: How did the enemies and prison guards of Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari عليه السلام react to his worship and presence?
ai.summary: This report describes how even harsh guards appointed over Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali عليه السلام were transformed by witnessing his intense worship, salat (prayer), fasting, and spiritual presence. It highlights his sanctity and the failure of his opponents to diminish his rank despite imprisonment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Ibrahim Bin Musa Bin Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abdul Ghaffar who said,

‘The Abbasides came over to Salih Bin Waseyf (the prison warden), and (also) Salih Bin Ali and others from the deviants from these areas came over to Salih Bin Waseyf, during the imprisonment of Abu Muhammadasws (11th Imamasws). So Salih said to them, ‘And what can I do, and I had allocated two men from the evillest as I was able upon finding upon himasws, but they came to a great matter from the worship and the Salat and the Fasting. So I said to these two, ‘What is it regarding himasws?’ So they both said, ‘What can we say about a man who is Fasting during the day and is standing (for Salat) during the night, all of it, not speaking nor pre-occupying (with anything else)? And whenever we look at himasws, our bodies tremble and (something) enters into us what we have no control over ourselves’. So when they heard that, they left disappointed’.
en.sarwar: 22. Ishaq has said that narrated to Muhammad ibn al-Qasim abu al-‘Ayna’ al-Hashimi, the slave of ‘Abd al-Samad ibn Ali ‘Ataqa the following.

“Often time I would go to see abu Muhammad (a.s.). When in his presence I would feel thirsty but I would feel shy, out of respect for him, to ask for water but he would call the people of his household to bring water for me. Often times I would think to myself of leaving and he would say, “Young man, bring his horse.”
